title: Banking, Loans and Keeping Your Money Safe
summary: UPI and OTP fraud, loans and interest, CIBIL, recovery agents, credit cards and the basics of income tax.
sectionRefs: Reserve Bank of India - Fair Practices Code and recovery agent rules

body.text: Most bank fraud does not need hacking. It only needs you to trust a caller, click a link, or share an OTP. A few simple rules keep your money safe.
🚨 Keep your money safe: UPI and OTP

items: Never share your OTP, PIN, CVV or password with anyone. No bank or official will ever ask for them.
To 'receive money', you never need to enter your PIN. Entering a PIN sends money out.
Do not scan a QR code to receive money.
Do not install screen-sharing or remote-access apps (apps that let someone else see or control your phone) for a 'bank officer'.
Check your account statement often.

body.text: 💳 If money leaves your account without your permission

items: Tell your bank at once. Ask them to freeze the account and dispute the transaction (challenge the payment).
Call the cyber helpline 1930. Also report it on cybercrime.gov.in.
Give the bank a written complaint. Get a receipt or acknowledgement.
If it is not solved, complain to the RBI Ombudsman (an official who settles bank complaints).
Read the loan agreement. Look at the interest rate, EMI (the monthly payment), processing fee, prepayment penalty and foreclosure terms (rules for closing the loan early).
Interest can be fixed or floating. A fixed rate stays the same. A floating rate changes with the market.
A guarantor (a person who promises to pay if the borrower does not) must pay if the borrower stops paying. Never sign as a guarantor without thinking it through.
Your CIBIL score shows how well you have repaid loans in the past. It decides whether you get a loan, and at what interest rate.
Check your credit report often for errors and for loans opened in your name.
The CIBIL score ranges from 300 to 900.

body.text: 🏦 What recovery agents can and cannot do

items: Recovery agents (people hired to collect a loan) may contact you. But they cannot threaten, abuse or harass you or your family.
They must not use force. They must not contact you at odd hours.
If they harass you, complain to your bank and to the RBI Ombudsman.
Check your statement for hidden charges, yearly fees and interest on money you have not paid.
Use only digital lending apps that the RBI controls. Apps that are not controlled can cheat you and misuse your data.
Interest is charged on the unpaid balance, and paying only the minimum keeps the debt growing.
Never pay into a personal account for a loan, tax or investment 'fee'.
Form 16 (from your employer), AIS and Form 26AS show your income and the TDS (tax already cut from your pay).
If your income is above the basic exemption limit (the amount on which you pay no tax), you usually must file an income tax return.
File on the official portal incometax.gov.in. Never pay money to a 'tax agent' into a personal account.
For most people, the income tax return is due by 31 July.

body.text: Missed calls and messages that make you panic ('your account will be blocked') are a common trick. Slow down. Check through the official app or the bank branch.
RBI rules limit how much you must pay for transactions you did not authorise. But this works only if you report quickly. If you delay, you may lose more.
Keep the SMS, email and complaint reference numbers. They prove when you reported the problem.

items: Under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021, you must first complain to the bank.
If the bank does not resolve it within 30 days, you can go to the RBI Ombudsman.

body.text: 💳 Unauthorised transactions: zero liability if you report fast

items: Under RBI rules, you have ZERO liability for an unauthorised electronic transaction if you report it within 3 working days.
If you delay, your own share of the loss can increase.

body.text: 🏦 Recovery agents: what the Fair Practices Code allows

items: Recovery agents must follow the RBI Fair Practices Code.
No threats or abuse.
No calling at unreasonable hours (broadly, not before 7 am or after 7 pm).
No contacting your family or neighbours about the loan.

body.text: 🏦 Credit cards: why the minimum payment grows your debt

items: Interest is charged on the unpaid balance.
Paying only the minimum keeps the debt growing.

practicalSteps: Never share OTP, PIN, CVV or passwords.
Report a fraudulent transaction to your bank as fast as you can.
Read the loan agreement before you sign. Never become a guarantor without understanding the risk.
If the bank does not solve your complaint within 30 days, go to the RBI Ombudsman.
exceptions: If the fraud happened because you shared your details, or were very careless, you may have to pay more.
If you report late, RBI rules may make you pay more of the loss.

faqs.q: Will the bank refund my money?
faqs.a: If you report quickly and were not careless, RBI rules say you pay little or nothing. The bank must solve your complaint within a fixed time.

faqs.q: Can a recovery agent call me at any time?
faqs.a: No. Agents must follow RBI rules about how and when they can call. If they threaten or harass you, complain to your bank and the RBI Ombudsman.

misconceptions.myth: If the bank's app shows the transaction, I cannot dispute it.
misconceptions.fact: You can and should dispute any transaction you did not authorise. Do it in writing to the bank.
